newsitem.title: USA: Nevada voters approve limits on tax increases.
newsitem.headline: Nevada voters approve limits on tax increases.

text.p: A Nevada ballot initiative that could limit the ability of the legislature to increase taxes was overwhelmingly approved by voters on Tuesday, according to election returns.
Under Question 11, a two-thirds majority vote of both houses of the state legislature would be required for passage of any bill or joint resolution that would increase public revenue in any form.
With roughly 95 percent of the vote counted, the measure had the support of nearly 70 percent of voters, with 30 percent opposed, election officials said.
Nevada voters also approved Question 16, which would require each house of the legislature to consider and approve twice any bill that imposes or increases a tax or assessment.
With 95 percent of the vote counted, Question 16 was supported by 60.9 percent, with 39.1 percent opposed.

Voters also backed Question 12, which will allow the state to issue $20 million of general obligation bonds to control erosion at Lake Tahoe, and Question 1, which would prohibit the state from borrowing money from public employees' retirement funds.
